note: Access profiles for the Cognition.X platforms: 20 learner types spanning learning differences, disabilities and learning states. THESE ARE SUPPORT PROFILES, NEVER DIAGNOSES — a profile is chosen by the learner and their family, can be combined, changed or removed at any time, and lives only in their own browser. The platform adapts pacing, step size, break cadence and check formats; it never labels a person, never gates content, and never shares a profile anywhere. Terminology follows common community preference (identity-first for autistic and Deaf learners, person-first elsewhere); accommodations are drawn from widely used universal-design and classroom-access practice and are options to try, not prescriptions. Every transfer check in the dataset can be demonstrated in an alternative format without losing what it proves — the capability is the constant; the format is the variable.

types.name: Learners with dyslexia
types.lens: Strong reasoning with print that fights back — decoding costs effort that comprehension doesn't.
helps: read-aloud or audio for any long text
fonts, spacing and short lines that reduce visual crowding
extra time with no ceremony
notes photographed, never recopied

flow.checkAlt: demonstrate orally, by diagram, or by doing — never gated on reading speed

types.classroom: Pre-teach key vocabulary; never call for cold reading aloud; grade the thinking, not the spelling.
types.home: Audiobooks count as reading; read the check aloud together and let them answer out loud.

types.name: Learners with dysgraphia
types.lens: Ideas outrun the pen — transcription, not thinking, is the bottleneck.
strengths: verbal reasoning ahead of the page
strong writing by voice or keyboard
helps: typing, dictation or scribing for anything long
diagrams and photos in place of copied notes
reduced-copying worksheets
pen grips and slant boards where they help

flow.checkAlt: say it, type it, demonstrate it, or have a scribe — handwriting is never the check

types.classroom: Provide the notes; assess the content of writing separately from its mechanics.
types.home: Let them dictate the log while you or a device writes; keep pencil work short and chosen.

types.name: Learners with dyscalculia
types.lens: Number sense needs scaffolds — quantity, sequence and mental math cost more than reasoning does.
strengths: strategy once the arithmetic is externalized
helps: number lines, hundred charts and manipulatives at every age
calculator for computation inside bigger tasks
one operation at a time, written steps
real objects before abstract symbols

flow.checkAlt: demonstrate with manipulatives or a calculator in hand — the reasoning is the check, not mental arithmetic

types.classroom: Anchor every computation in a picture or object; never time arithmetic drills for this learner.
types.home: Cook, measure and shop together — jobsite math with real material is the strongest path in.

types.name: Learners with ADHD
types.lens: Attention follows interest and urgency — energy is an asset that needs structure, not suppression.
strengths: energy that lifts a whole crew
helps: short work sprints with visible timers
movement breaks that are legal and frequent
one instruction at a time, in writing
fidgets and standing work without comment

flow.checkAlt: checks broken into short, timed rounds with movement between

types.classroom: Front-load novelty; let them work standing or moving; the bench beats the lecture every time.
types.home: Body first — movement before homework; agree the sprint length together and honor the break.

types.name: Autistic learners
types.lens: Deep focus, honest communication and pattern mastery — with a real cost to surprise, noise and unwritten rules.
strengths: depth and precision in chosen domains
helps: predictable routines and advance notice of change
written rules that mean what they say
quiet workspace or ear protection available
special interests welcomed as doorways into any track

flow.checkAlt: checks scheduled in advance, in a known format, in a low-sensory setting; scripts and interests welcome

types.classroom: Post the plan and keep it; explain the why; never force eye contact or group work as the price of learning.
types.home: Use the interest as the engine — any theme can be reached through what they already love.

types.name: Learners with auditory processing differences
types.lens: Hearing is fine; spoken language in noise arrives scrambled — print and pictures carry better.
strengths: strong with written and visual input
careful checking once input is clear
helps: instructions in writing, every time
one speaker at a time, facing the learner
quiet seating away from hum and hallway
repeat-back to confirm, without penalty

flow.checkAlt: written or demonstrated instructions; oral checks in a quiet room, face to face

types.classroom: Say it, then show it written; check understanding by asking them to do, not to repeat.
types.home: Turn the TV off during instructions; one step at a time, and write the list down together.

types.name: Learners with visual processing differences
types.lens: Sight is fine; dense pages, crowded diagrams and copying from the board cost extra decoding.
helps: clean layouts — one thing per page region
enlarged print and strong contrast
rulers, windows and markers to track lines
verbal walk-throughs of any diagram

flow.checkAlt: oral and hands-on checks; any diagram also described aloud

types.classroom: Hand out what's on the board; declutter worksheets; teach diagrams by talking through them.
types.home: Read tables and maps aloud together; let the hands learn what the page makes hard.

types.name: Learners with speech and language differences
types.lens: Understanding and expression can each need time — fluency of speech is not depth of thought.
helps: wait time without rescue or interruption
alternative expression — writing, pointing, AAC devices honored fully
simplified instruction language, normal content
never grading ideas on pronunciation or fluency

flow.checkAlt: demonstrate, write, sign or use AAC — the check is the capability, never the speech

types.classroom: Give the floor and the time; treat AAC as the learner's voice, because it is.
types.home: Model without correcting mid-sentence; celebrate the message, not the delivery.

types.name: Deaf and hard-of-hearing learners
types.lens: Full learners in a hearing-built room — access is visual, and interpretation or captioning is a right, not a favor.
helps: captions on every video, no exceptions
interpreters or transcription for live instruction where used
clear sightlines to the speaker's face
visual alerts alongside every audio cue

flow.checkAlt: checks delivered and answered visually — signed, written or demonstrated

types.classroom: Face the class when speaking; repeat peers' questions; put every announcement in writing.
types.home: Learn the signs the learner uses; watch captioned material together and discuss in their language.

types.name: Blind and low-vision learners
types.lens: The world arrives by touch, sound and description — materials must be built for hands and ears, not adapted as an afterthought.
helps: screen readers, braille or large print as the learner uses them
tactile models and real objects for anything spatial
verbal description of every visual
consistent physical layout of rooms and materials

flow.checkAlt: checks by touch, sound and speech; every visual artifact has a described or tactile equivalent

types.classroom: Say what you write as you write it; hand them the object the others are looking at.
types.home: Narrate the work as you do it together; label the home's materials the way the learner reads.

types.name: Learners with mobility and motor differences
types.lens: The plan is fine; the built world and the tools need adjusting — access is an engineering problem, not a lowering of the bar.
helps: reachable, stable workstations
adapted grips, jigs and fixtures
extra transition time between spaces
a role in every crew task — director, checker, caller

flow.checkAlt: checks adapted in tooling and position, or performed by directing another's hands step by step

types.classroom: Fix the bench, not the expectation; the learner who directs a lift correctly has passed the lift check.
types.home: Rig the task to the body — clamp it, raise it, slow it — and let them run the job.

types.name: Learners with chronic illness and fatigue
types.lens: Capacity is real but variable — the good day and the flare day need different plans, both honorable.
helps: flexible deadlines and attendance without penalty
work chunked to survive interruption
rest as a scheduled part of the plan
catch-up paths that never punish absence

flow.checkAlt: checks schedulable on good days, splittable across sessions, never forfeited by absence

types.classroom: Plan for the flare in advance; record the bench so a missed day is watchable, not lost.
types.home: Follow the energy honestly; a short session completed beats a long one endured.

types.name: Anxiety-affected learners
types.lens: The skill is present; the alarm system fires early — safety and predictability unlock what pressure locks.
helps: advance notice of what will be asked
low-stakes rehearsal before any audience
an agreed exit-and-return signal
grading that never hinges on one performance

flow.checkAlt: checks rehearsed first, witnessed by a chosen person, retried without record

types.classroom: Never cold-call; post what tomorrow holds; treat the retry as the design, not the exception.
types.home: Name the worry, shrink the first step, and let them teach you — teaching back is safe mastery.

types.name: Trauma-affected learners
types.lens: The nervous system learned to guard first — regulation comes before curriculum, relationship before correction.
helps: predictable routines and warned transitions
choices that restore control
a known safe adult and a quiet reset space
correction in private, connection in public

flow.checkAlt: checks with a trusted witness, in a familiar space, with control over the when

types.classroom: Connect before you correct; the behavior is a signal, not the student; keep your promises exactly.
types.home: Consistency is the curriculum; small kept promises rebuild what unpredictability took.

types.name: Learners with intellectual disabilities
types.lens: Learning is real and rightful at every pace — smaller steps, more practice, the same dignity and the same real material.
helps: one skill at a time, concretely modeled
many spaced repetitions without shame
real tasks with visible purpose
partial credit for partial steps — every rung counts

flow.checkAlt: checks split into their smallest honest steps, each demonstrated and celebrated on real material

types.classroom: Teach the step, not the abstraction; the same transfer check, reached by a longer, prouder road.
types.home: Real chores are the curriculum — the table set right is a check passed.

types.name: Gifted and twice-exceptional learners
types.lens: Asynchronous by design — years ahead in one lane, age-typical or supported in another, bored by repetition that others need.
strengths: depth of interest beyond the syllabus
helps: compacting — test out of what is already known
depth and mentorship over extra worksheets
supports for the other exceptionality honored fully
peers who share the interest, whatever their age

flow.checkAlt: checks at the band the evidence supports, not the birthday; 2e supports never revoked for being 'smart enough'

types.classroom: Pre-assess and compact; feed the interest with the real thing — the working expert, the real problem.
types.home: Follow the obsession to its real-world floor — the hall, the lab, the archive.

types.name: Multilingual learners new to English
types.lens: Full intellect arriving through a second language — the accent is not the mind, and the first language is an asset, not an obstacle.
helps: content in plain English with visuals
the first language welcomed for thinking and drafting
vocabulary pre-taught with pictures and objects
pairing with a same-language peer where possible

flow.checkAlt: demonstrate in any language or by doing; English develops alongside the capability, never as its gate

types.classroom: Teach the content and the language of the content, separately and on purpose; honor the first language aloud.
types.home: Keep the home language strong — it is the foundation the second one stands on.

types.name: Learners with executive function and working-memory differences
types.lens: The engine is strong; the dashboard needs externalizing — plans, sequences and reminders belong on paper, not in the head.
strengths: strong reasoning once material is externalized
helps: checklists and visible schedules for everything
one instruction at a time, in order, in writing
materials stored in one labeled place
external timers instead of internal guessing

flow.checkAlt: checks with the checklist in hand — using the scaffold is the skill, not cheating

types.classroom: Externalize everything; teach the system, grade the work; the learner who runs their checklist has learned the job.
types.home: One launch pad by the door, one list on the fridge, one step at a time — build the habit as a family.

types.name: Learners with sensory processing differences
types.lens: The volume knobs are set differently — light, sound, touch and motion can flood or under-fill, and regulation is the first skill.
strengths: honest signals when the room is wrong
helps: sensory tools without stigma — headphones, fidgets, chewables
seating choice away from triggers
movement or deep-pressure breaks on request
warning before sensory events (bells, drills, crowds)

flow.checkAlt: checks in a sensory-safe setting chosen with the learner; regulation breaks never reset progress

types.classroom: Audit the room's noise and light; make the tools ordinary; believe the signal before the meltdown.
types.home: Build the calm kit together and practice using it before it's needed.

types.name: Learners who process at a deliberate pace
types.lens: Thorough, not slow — the answer arrives whole, later; speed limits measure the clock, not the mind.
helps: extended time as the default, not an event
fewer problems at full depth
wait time after every question
no public races, ever

flow.checkAlt: untimed checks; mastery shown on fewer, deeper items

types.classroom: Ask, then count to ten silently; assess with five deep problems instead of twenty shallow ones.
types.home: Protect the finish — the task completed thoroughly today beats three rushed.
